text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
*Cabinet under-secretary Vitalino Canas admits that the Estorial Formula One track, in which the government bought a controlling stake, will probably never turn a profit.

*After buying 30 percent of the Argentine company Bauen, Efacec is preparing investments in Latin America and the Far East totalling one billion escudos. The results of the company in the first semestre of 1997 may be over one billion escudos due to the restructuring of the company's liabilities.

*Building company Grao Para will develop a real estate project around the Estoril autodrome, similar to that in Silverstone, England. The participation of an oriental group as partner in this 40 billion escudos project is certain.

*According to the Under-Secretary for Industry and Energy Jose Penedos, taxes on fuel products should be lowered and measures should be taken for fuel tax harmonization within the European Community. He also said the second phase for the privatisation of EDP-Electriciade de Portugal will only occur after June 1998.
*Foreign investors have been investing on Lisbon stock market attracted by expectations of profits on the banking sector, whose results will be reported tomorrow.

*The government is counting on reduced interest payments and a profit from the social security system to ensure its 2.9 percent budget deficit target for 1997, Prime Minister Antonio Guterres is quoted as saying.
*The banks Banco Espirito Santo and Caixa Geral de Depositos are interested in the privatisation of Brasilian bank Banespa.
*According to government figures, Portuguese investment through to the end of 1998 totals 180 billion escudos, involving 30 companies.
